newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic daily power firms; deferreds dip.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic daily power firms; deferreds dip.

text.p: Day-ahead bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic firmed Wednesday on frigid weather settling over the region, while deferred values softened in line with lower NYMEX natural gas futures.
"It's mainly the cold weather," replied one power trader when asked about the factors behind the rise in daily prices.

Firm, peak PJM electricity for Thursday (excluding transmission costs) was mostly traded in a $30.00-$32.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range with deals reportedly heard as high as $34.00. Today's quote was higher than Tuesday's $29.50-$30.50 for delivery today.
Firm, off-peak PJM for Thursday also rose, quoted at $15.00-$17.00 against $14.50-$15.50 Tuesday.
Buying interests for daily power have risen with the approach of the refueling outage of the 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick 2 nuclear power unit, market sources said.
The Pottsdam, Pa. generating unit which was running at roughly 75 percent power is scheduled to begin shutdown late Thursday for a 25-day refueling and maintenance program.

In the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district, temperatures are expected to run slightly below normal before the weekend with chance of light snow Thursday and snowshowers Saturday. Then, readings would drop to six to 12 degrees F below normal Saturday through Monday.
February PJM electricity firmed to $24.40-$29.60 from Tuesday's $29.25-$29.50.
March PJM power stepped down to $24.25-$24.45 from $24.35-$24.55 Tuesday.
PJM deliveries for April and May slipped to $22.00-$22.20 from Tuesday's $22.10-$22.40.
June power prices in PJM dipped to $25.00-$25.15 from $25.10-$25.35 Tuesday.
July/August PJM deliveries fell to $30.00-$30.20 from Tuesday's $30.35-$30.50.
PJM electricity for the third-quarter was pegged at $27.75-$28.00, while fourth-quarter PJM dropped to $23.75-$24.00 from $23.90-$24.20 Tuesday.
Swing gas prices at the Philadelphia city gate were notationally assessed near $4.00 per million British thermal units, the upper end of Tuesday's quote.
As of 1241 EST, NYMEX March Henry Hub gas futures fell 4.1 cents to $2.505, testing key support after Tuesday's losses.

Separately, Salem nuclear units 1 and 2, each at 1,078 MW, were added to Nuclear Regulatory Commission's watch list of facilities requiring increased regulatory attention to ensure their safe and reliable operation.
The Salem units in Salem, N.J., are jointly owned by Public Service Electric and Gas Co, PECO Energy Co, Delmarva Power & Light Co and Atlantic Energy Inc.
